topic: Extended VTE prophylaxis after abdominal cancer surgery

audits.title: EP-67 An Audit of extended Venous Thromboembolic Prophylaxis for major Laparotomy in a District General Hospital, Are We Compliance With NICE guidelines?
audits.standard: NICE: extended VTE prophylaxis (LMWH for 28 days) after major abdominal surgery
audits.setting: District general hospital, Southport and Ormskirk NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 189 (61%) discharged with extended VTE prophylaxis; 121 (39%) did not receive it.

audits.other_findings: Of the 121 without extended prophylaxis, 2 developed VTE (one DVT and PE, one DVT).
audits.citation: Elshafey T, Azam M, Satchidanand R. EP-67 An Audit of extended Venous Thromboembolic Prophylaxis for major Laparotomy in a District General Hospital, Are We Compliance With NICE guidelines?. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_5). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac245.019.

audits.title: TU5.8 Audit on Adherence to NICE Guidelines for VTE Prophylaxis in Patients Undergoing Surgery for Appendicitis
audits.standard: NICE NG89: pharmacological VTE prophylaxis for a minimum of 7 days after abdominal surgery and mechanical prophylaxis from admission
audits.setting: Stockport NHS Foundation Trust, patients over 16 undergoing surgery for appendicitis

cycle1.result: VTE risk assessment completed in 12 (52.2%); TEDS 15/23 (65.2%); enoxaparin 18 (78.2%); 4 (17.4%) had no prophylaxis; none prescribed seven days of pharmacological prophylaxis.

audits.other_findings: Mean hospital stay 2.8 days; prophylaxis often missed in short stays.
audits.citation: Devarakonda S, Shuttleworth P, Clark E. TU5.8 Audit on Adherence to NICE Guidelines for VTE Prophylaxis in Patients Undergoing Surgery for Appendicitis. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_5). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac248.051.

audits.title: TH8.5 VTE Pharmacological Prophylaxis in Oesophagogastric Cancer Resection Patients: A Triple Cycle Closed Loop Audit Against NICE Guidance NG89
audits.standard: NICE NG89: 28 days extended VTE pharmacological prophylaxis after major abdominal cancer surgery

cycle1.result: 14% compliance; median prophylaxis duration 7 days; correct weight-based dose in 89%.

audits.intervention: Unit protocol change to 14 days and then 28 days postoperative prophylaxis, with clinician education

cycle2.result: 91% compliance; median duration 28 days; correct dose in 100%.

audits.other_findings: Three cycles: cycle 2 (2019-21) had 26% compliance and median 23 days; 2 bleeding and 1 VTE event in cycles 1 and 2, none in cycle 3.
audits.citation: Baxter J, Room H, Parsley C, Smith B, Sechante C. TH8.5 VTE Pharmacological Prophylaxis in Oesophagogastric Cancer Resection Patients: A Triple Cycle Closed Loop Audit Against NICE Guidance NG89. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_5). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac248.270.

audits.title: FTP3.13 Patients undergoing major abdominal cancer surgery should receive 28 days of VTE prophylaxis: a single-centre audit of patients treated surgically for colorectal cancer
audits.standard: NICE 2018: 28 days of post-operative VTE prophylaxis after major abdominal cancer surgery
audits.setting: Bedfordshire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust; patients treated surgically for colorectal cancer

cycle1.result: 84% compliance overall (88% elective, 55% emergency). Documented plan for extended prophylaxis in 82% of recipients and 12% of non-recipients.

audits.intervention: Planned: education, posters and improved electronic discharge processes; second cycle being collected prospectively from 25/01/2023.
audits.other_findings: 89% of operations were elective and 11% emergency; compliance was lower in emergency cases.
audits.citation: Epanomeritakis I, Radhakrishnan R, Bevan K. FTP3.13 Patients undergoing major abdominal cancer surgery should receive 28 days of VTE prophylaxis: a single-centre audit of patients treated surgically for colorectal cancer. audits.title: OGC SO12 - Extended Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis in Postoperative Oesophagogastric Cancer Patients: A Completed Audit
audits.standard: NICE: extended pharmacological VTE prophylaxis for 28 days after major abdominal cancer surgery
audits.setting: Oesophago-gastric unit, Lancashire Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, Preston

cycle1.result: Pre-2014: 13/92 (14.1%) discharged with 28-day prophylaxis; post-2014: 423/490 (86.3%) (p<0.05); VTE 0.17%

audits.intervention: Trust-wide policy of 28-day extended VTE prophylaxis after discharge adopted in 2014

cycle2.result: 63/68 (92.6%) received prophylaxis (86.3% to 92.6%, p=0.145); VTE 0%; no bleeding readmissions

audits.other_findings: No readmissions for bleeding complications in either period.
audits.citation: Kuan J, Turner P, Pursnani K, Ward J, Shetty V. OGC SO12 - Extended Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis in Postoperative Oesophagogastric Cancer Patients: A Completed Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_9). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae271.137.

audits.title: Improving adherence to guidelines for extended venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in patients with colorectal cancer.
audits.standard: Local EVTEP guidelines based on NICE (28 days LMWH after colorectal cancer surgery)
audits.setting: Colorectal surgery unit, Bristol Royal Infirmary, inner city teaching hospital

cycle1.result: 11% of at-risk patients identified in pre-operative assessment clinic; 44% prescribed EVTEP at discharge

audits.intervention: Education of the multidisciplinary team and presentation of audit results after each cycle
audits.other_findings: A second cycle (April to May 2012, n=17) also had 100% prescribed at discharge; identification of at-risk patients and patient education improved.
audits.citation: Patel M, Harris M, Tapply I, Longman R. Improving adherence to guidelines for extended venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in patients with colorectal cancer. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2014;2(2):u200573.w1062. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u200573.w1062. PMID: 26734218.

audits.title: Improving prescribing of extended prophylaxis for venous thromboembolism at discharge in patients who underwent surgery for colorectal cancer.
audits.standard: NICE guidance on extended VTE prophylaxis at discharge after colorectal cancer surgery
audits.setting: Department of Surgery, The County Hospital, Hereford

cycle1.result: Cyclical 4-monthly decline in compliance coinciding with foundation doctor rotations

audits.intervention: Six multidisciplinary interventions including education of health professionals

cycle2.result: 100% compliance with prescribing extended VTE prophylaxis at discharge

audits.other_findings: 181 elective and 29 emergency patients; no VTE events at 30 days.
audits.citation: Ong CT, Leung E, Shah AP. Improving prescribing of extended prophylaxis for venous thromboembolism at discharge in patients who underwent surgery for colorectal cancer. Br J Hosp Med (Lond). 2020;81(11):1-7. doi:10.12968/hmed.2020.0405. PMID: 33263480.

audits.title: Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) Prophylaxis on Discharge Following Major Cancer Surgery in the Abdomen: Improving Compliance With National Guidelines.
audits.standard: NICE guidelines: 28-day extended post-discharge VTE prophylaxis after major abdominal cancer surgery
audits.setting: District general hospital (elective abdominal cancer surgery)

cycle1.result: VTE assessment and inpatient prophylaxis 100%; full 28-day post-discharge prophylaxis 49.1%; 24.5% no prophylaxis after discharge; 20.8% exceeded recommended duration.

audits.intervention: Teaching for junior doctors, posters in relevant departments and reminders in electronic patient records.

cycle2.result: 81.25% completed prescribed course; 14.8% inpatient-only prophylaxis; 3.7% exceeded 28 days; overall non-compliance fell from 50.9% to 18.5%.

audits.citation: Iqbal H. Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) Prophylaxis on Discharge Following Major Cancer Surgery in the Abdomen: Improving Compliance With National Guidelines. Cureus. 2024;16(11):e73186. doi:10.7759/cureus.73186. PMID: 39651012.
